newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mixed amid weather jitters, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mixed amid weather jitters, funds.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mixed amid weather jitters with fund buying buoying the market to fresh five-month highs, traders said.
"Funds were buying again," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co. "They did at least 20 million today."

The fund purchases were estimated at least 20 million bushels but late commercial selling limited the advances and the market already was beginning to deal with uncertainty about the 1997 U.S. crop weather. Wet weather and flooding led to early concerns about delays in seeding the corn crop.
March set a session high of $3.08-3/4 per bushel. That's a a new five-month peak and the highest level for that contract since $3.10 was touched on October 2.

Traders said the posting of no deliveries on the March contract also aided the case for bulls along with the persistent firm tone in the soy complex. Soybeans rallied sharply Monday and added to those gains Tuesday.
"The path of least resistance is up so why try to get tricky here," a trader said.
Corn closed one cent per bushel higher to 2-1/2 cents lower, with March up one at $3.03-3/4.
Technicians early Tuesday cited first resistance in the March at $3.04 and second resistance at $3.07-1/2. The session high for March was $3.08-3/4.
First support was at $3.00-1/2 and second support was at $2.97. The session low was $3.01-3/4.

Chartists said the four and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish signals for the corn market. The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for the March closed at 87 percent. The trade views a market as overbought with an RSI of 70 or more and oversold at 30 or less.

Cargill Inc bought two million bushels of May and sold five million bushels of March, traders said. Merrill Lynch Futures bought six million May, Prudential Securities and Refco Inc each bought three million bushels of May and three million bushels of July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 100,000 contracts, above the 96,802 traded Monday.

In corn options, Rand Financial bought 800 May $3.00 puts and sold 800 July $3.40 calls at eight cents, Smith Barney sold 650 May $3.70 calls at one cent, sold 400 May $3.00 puts at eight to 8-1/2 cents and sold 500 May $3.10 puts at 12-1/2 to 13-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 25,000 contracts, below the 26,948 traded Monday.
